    The cutoff criterion for pretorsion theories #

    Theorem 6.5 of the manuscript: the pair (T_β, F_α) of a quotient-closed and a subobject-closed subcategory of mod Λ_n is a pretorsion theory iff in every column d, either α d = 0 (the column lies entirely in F_α), or the pivot row e = α d - 1 satisfies d < β e (so M_{e,d} ∈ T_β) and no earlier row a < e has cutoff β a = d (Criterion).

    The proof follows the manuscript. For the "if" direction it suffices, by the decomposition into intervals and the compatibility of short preexact sequences with direct sums, to verify the trace–reject condition (2.4) on each interval M_{c,d}; this uses the computation of traces and rejects of intervals and the three steps of the manuscript's proof (beta_lt_of_criterion is Step 1). The "only if" direction uses Corollary 2.13.

    Consequently the pretorsion theories of mod Λ_n correspond to cutoff pairs satisfying the criterion (pretorsionEquiv), and there are finitely many.
